This starts to get spooky when you realize that we have one in containment, but since they hide perfectly there could be a huge number of these out in the wild and no one would know it. Maybe they are the natural predators of SCP-966, part of a whole invisible ecology.

Alternatively, its species competes with 966. It uses the similar strategy of hunting by driving people nuts. It hides itself from everyone else for days or weeks, and when the target finally snaps and kills himself it scavenges the corpse.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Kinda neat? Big spider thingy that hides just out of the corner of your eye and who knows why. That is just the sort of creepy thing SCPs should be doing.

I think part of the problem is that it's missing some of the investigation into "why". I mean, sure it's secured and contained, and thus the basic function of SCP has been carried out, but it usually doesn't stop there. Why haven't they added stop-motion cameras to its room to at least try and get a better look at it? Could mention that they tried and it could apparently sense the electrical signals of the cameras because it became distraught and violent, smashing itself against the walls of the cell repeatedly, so the cameras were shut off to keep it from killing itself or being driven to break out, whichever came first.

The very basic research into this thing should at least consist of trying to find out "Is this a Unique SCP or a Species SCP?"
